title: Operation Polo and the annexation of Hyderabad
summary: On 12–13 September 1948 the Indian Army invaded the princely state of Hyderabad, ruled by the Nizam. Its forces surrendered within days (18 September in one account), and India announced the state merged into the Union on 23 September. A mission set up at Nehru's wish reportedly estimated 27,000 to 40,000 deaths in communal violence during and after the operation.

uncertainty.note: Invasion given as 12–13 September (EBSCO; the id uses 13 September). Surrender is 18 September in EBSCO, while other accounts say 17 September. Violence continued after the fighting.

as_recorded.value: On September 12-13, 1948, the Indian Army invaded Hyderabad
the Hyderabadi forces surrendered on September 18

where.modern_name: Hyderabad and surrounding territory, Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, India
where.historical_name: Hyderabad State, a princely state under the Nizam, Asaf Jahi dynasty

importance.justification: Ended princely rule in a large state of the subcontinent and integrated it into India, with a contested toll of civilian deaths.

audience_note: Involves mass communal killing, rape and religious violence against civilians in the aftermath; casualty figures are disputed and reports differ on who was responsible.

related.because: After independence India viewed Hyderabad's separate status as an anomaly, and its leaders pressed for military action.

sources.title: REVIEW: The Destruction of Hyderabad by A.G. Noorani

reviewer_note: Death toll is contested: the 27,000–40,000 figure is reported through a book review by a critic of the operation; official figures are lower and I did not open them. Pin is the capital city; the fighting covered the state border.
